# Arrival Alerts

Arrival alerts tell you when a vessel reports a new position or a revised arrival time. You choose which vessels to watch and when to hear about them. Harbourlight does the rest.

## What an alert tells you

Each alert names the vessel and what changed. That change is either a new reported position or a revised estimated arrival time. Use the alert to plan berth work, customs paperwork, and staffing before the vessel gets close.

## Choose your vessels and timing

Pick the vessels you want to follow. For each one, set how close to arrival the alert should fire. You can pick any of these:

- 24 hours before arrival
- 6 hours before arrival
- 1 hour before arrival
- On berth

You can set more than one. A vessel can alert you at 24 hours and again at 1 hour if that helps you plan.

## Choose how you get alerts

Alerts reach you three ways:

- **Email**
- **SMS**
- **Another system**

Pick one or several. Email and SMS are ready to use. The next section covers alerts to another system.

## Send alerts to another system

You can have Harbourlight deliver alerts straight into your own software. Give Harbourlight a URL. When an alert fires, Harbourlight sends the alert to that URL.

The alert's contents arrive as a structured message. Each message carries:

- the vessel id
- the alert type
- the new estimated arrival time, in UTC
- a signature

The signature lets your system confirm the message came from Harbourlight and was not changed on the way. Harbourlight builds it from the raw message body and a shared secret that only you and Harbourlight hold. It travels in the `X-Harbourlight-Signature` header. Check it against the raw body before you trust the alert.

If your system does not answer, Harbourlight tries again. It retries up to 5 times and waits longer between tries. If all tries fail, Harbourlight marks the delivery as failed. You can see failed deliveries in the alert history for 30 days. Check that history if your system was down and you need to know what you missed.

## Set quiet hours

You can set quiet hours for yourself. Alerts that fall inside them are held. Harbourlight sends the held alerts when your quiet hours end. This keeps overnight position updates off your phone until you are back on shift.

**On berth** alerts are the exception. They always go out right away, even inside quiet hours. A vessel reaching the berth is time-critical, so you hear about it at once.

Quiet hours are set per person. Your quiet hours do not change what your colleagues receive.

## Set it up

1. Open the vessel you want to follow.
2. Turn on arrival alerts for that vessel.
3. Choose your timings: 24 hours, 6 hours, 1 hour, on berth, or a mix.
4. Choose your channels: email, SMS, another system, or a mix.
5. To use another system, enter your URL and your shared secret.
6. Set your quiet hours if you want them.
7. Save.

Repeat for each vessel you track.

## Check your alert history

The alert history shows what Harbourlight sent and when. It also shows failed deliveries to another system for 30 days. Use it to confirm an alert went out, or to see why one did not reach your software.

## Tips

- Set a 24 hour alert for planning and a 1 hour alert for final prep.
- Keep on berth alerts on for vessels you meet at the quay.
- Store your shared secret somewhere safe. You need it to check each signature.
